title: Just washed it
setting: A Sunday morning in Kenta and Sora's flat. Kenta is making breakfast when Sora walks in with his hair looking different. Today Sora is seeing a movie with a girl he likes.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, sora, ohayou. are? kami kitta?
lines.ja: あ、ソラ、おはよう。あれ？髪切った？
lines.kana: あ、そら、おはよう。あれ？かみきった？
lines.english: Oh, morning, Sora. Huh? Did you get a haircut?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.ja: 切ってないよ。髪洗っただけ。
lines.kana: きってないよ。かみあらっただけ。
lines.english: Nope, didn't cut it. I just washed it.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e? kinou, kami kiri ni iku n ja nakatta?
lines.ja: え？昨日、髪切りに行くんじゃなかった？
lines.kana: え？きのう、かみきりにいくんじゃなかった？
lines.english: Huh? Weren't you going to get it cut yesterday?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ikenakatta. kinou wa shigoto ga isogashikute.
lines.ja: 行けなかった。昨日は仕事が忙しくて。
lines.kana: いけなかった。きのうはしごとがいそがしくて。
lines.english: Couldn't make it. Work was too busy yesterday.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: fuun. demo, kami aratta dake de kekkou kawaru ne.
lines.ja: ふーん。でも、髪洗っただけで結構変わるね。
lines.kana: ふーん。でも、かみあらっただけでけっこうかわるね。
lines.english: Huh. Still, just washing it makes quite a difference.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: datte kyou, ano ko to eiga miru n da.
lines.ja: だって今日、あの子と映画見るんだ。
lines.kana: だってきょう、あのことえいがみるんだ。
lines.english: Well, I'm seeing a movie with that girl today.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, dakara kami aratta n da. jaa, kao mo aratta?
lines.ja: え、だから髪洗ったんだ。じゃあ、顔も洗った？
lines.kana: え、だからかみあらったんだ。じゃあ、かおもあらった？
lines.english: Oh, so that's why you washed your hair! So, did you wash your face too?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: kao? a, mada da. aratte kuru!
lines.ja: 顔？あ、まだだ。洗ってくる！
lines.kana: かお？あ、まだだ。あらってくる！
lines.english: My face? Oh, not yet. I'll go wash it!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: kao aratte kita? un, ii ne.
lines.ja: 顔洗ってきた？うん、いいね。
lines.kana: かおあらってきた？うん、いいね。

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un. demo, tsume nagai yo. kittoki na yo.
lines.ja: うん。でも、爪長いよ。切っときなよ。
lines.kana: うん。でも、つめながいよ。きっときなよ。
lines.english: Yeah. But your nails are long. Cut them before you go.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e? a, honto da. tsume kiranakya.
lines.ja: え？あ、ほんとだ。爪切らなきゃ。
lines.kana: え？あ、ほんとだ。つめきらなきゃ。
lines.english: Huh? Oh, you're right. I need to cut my nails.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: gohan dekita yo. te aratte kite.
lines.ja: ご飯できたよ。手洗ってきて。
lines.kana: ごはんできたよ。てあらってきて。
lines.english: Breakfast is ready. Go wash your hands.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: okaasan ka yo. tsume kitte, te mo aratta yo.
lines.ja: お母さんかよ。爪切って、手も洗ったよ。
lines.kana: おかあさんかよ。つめきって、てもあらったよ。
lines.english: What are you, my mom? I cut my nails and washed my hands too.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: はいはい。じゃあ、どうぞ。
lines.kana: はいはい。じゃあ、どうぞ。

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: itadakimasu. a, kenta wa? kao aratta?
lines.ja: いただきます。あ、ケンタは？顔洗った？
lines.kana: いただきます。あ、けんたは？かおあらった？
lines.english: Thanks for the food. Oh, what about you, Kenta? Did you wash your face?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: boku? te wa aratta kedo, kao wa mada da.
lines.ja: 僕？手は洗ったけど、顔はまだだ。
lines.kana: ぼく？てはあらったけど、かおはまだだ。
lines.english: Me? I washed my hands, but not my face yet.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: okaasan mo, kao aratte kite ne.
lines.ja: お母さんも、顔洗ってきてね。
lines.kana: おかあさんも、かおあらってきてね。
lines.english: You too, Mom. Go wash your face.

choices.english: Sora only washed his hair, but Kenta thought he'd had it cut. Kenta checks him over before his movie date, then turns out not to have washed his own face.
Sora got his hair cut after work yesterday, and Kenta tells him to cut his nails before his movie date.
Kenta has a movie date today, so Sora checks him over and tells him to wash his face and cut his nails.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Kenta asks kami kitta? and Sora says kittenai yo, kami aratta dake (I didn't cut it, I just washed it). Lines 3-4: he meant to get it cut yesterday but couldn't (ikenakatta). Line 6: today he's seeing a movie with that girl. Lines 7-14: Kenta checks Sora's face, nails and hands. Lines 16-17: Sora asks Kenta the same question, and Kenta hasn't washed his face yet (kao wa mada da). B is wrong: Sora never got the haircut, because work was too busy (line 4). C swaps them: the date is Sora's (line 6), and it's Kenta who checks Sora over; Sora only turns the face question back on Kenta at the end.

questions.english: You've just got home. Kenta calls from the kitchen, "a, gohan dekita yo!" (Oh, food's ready!) Tell him you'll go and wash your hands first.
questions.answer: Say you'll go and wash your hands, with te (o) arau in the te-form plus kuru: te aratte kuru.

modelAnswers.english: Okay, I'll go wash my hands.

modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、手を洗ってきます。
modelAnswers.english: Then I'll go and wash my hands.

questions.explanation: Washing your hands is te o arau. Aratte kuru is 'go and wash, then come back', the same shape as Kenta's te aratte kite (line 13) and Sora's aratte kuru (line 8). Casual speech drops o (te aratte); the polite version keeps it. Sora answers Kenta in line 14 with te mo aratta yo (I washed my hands too), and Kenta uses it in line 17 (te wa aratta kedo). The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san or Satou-san.

questions.english: You've only just got up. Kenta asks, "ohayou. mada nemui?" (Morning. Still sleepy?) Say yes, and that you'll go and wash your face.
questions.answer: Say yes, then kao (o) aratte kuru: un, nemui. kao aratte kuru.

modelAnswers.ja: うん、眠い。顔洗ってくる。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm sleepy. I'll go wash my face.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, mada nemui kara, chotto kao aratte kuru.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、まだ眠いから、ちょっと顔洗ってくる。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, still sleepy, so I'll just go wash my face.

questions.explanation: Washing your face is kao o arau, with the same arau as hands and hair. Splashing your face is the standard way to wake yourself up, so aratte kuru (I'll go and wash it) is the natural reply. Kenta asks kao mo aratta? in line 7, Sora says aratte kuru! in line 8, and Kenta checks kao aratte kita? in line 9. At the end Sora sends Kenta off the same way: kao aratte kite ne (line 18).

questions.english: Kenta asks Sora if he got a haircut, and Sora answers "kittenai yo. kami aratta dake." What had Sora done to his hair?

choices.english: He'd had it trimmed just a little, so it barely looked different.
He'd cut it himself at home, because he couldn't get to the salon.
He'd only washed it; he hadn't cut it at all.

questions.explanation: Line 2: kittenai is 'I haven't cut it', and kami aratta dake is 'I just washed my hair'. Arau is the everyday verb for washing hair too; there's no separate shampoo verb. Kenta repeats it in line 5 (kami aratta dake de kekkou kawaru ne: just washing it makes quite a difference) and line 7 (dakara kami aratta n da). A is wrong: kittenai means he didn't cut it at all; even a small trim would be kitta (chotto kitta). B is wrong: he couldn't get to the salon (line 4: ikenakatta), but he didn't cut it anywhere. Washing was all he did.

questions.english: When Kenta first sees Sora, his hair looks different. What does Kenta ask him?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Huh? Did your hair get cut on you?
Huh? Did you get a haircut?
Huh? Did you wear your hair? (kita = wore)

questions.explanation: Line 1: kami kitta? is the stock 'did you get a haircut?'. Japanese says it even though a stylist does the cutting: line 3 shows Kenta thought Sora had gone to the salon (kami kiri ni iku). C uses kita, the past of the other kiru, 'wear' (fuku o kiru, kita). Cut is kitta, with the double t you hear as a tiny pause; wear is kita, with no pause. A, kirareta, is the passive. It makes the cut something done to you, the way you'd complain that a stylist took too much off. English 'have your hair cut' doesn't need a passive in Japanese; plain kitta covers a salon cut.

questions.english: Yuki phones while you're in the middle of cutting your nails. She asks, "moshimoshi? ima nani shiteru no?" (Hello? What are you up to right now?) Tell her.
questions.ja: もしもし？今何してるの？
questions.kana: もしもし？いまなにしてるの？
questions.answer: Say you're cutting your nails, with tsume (o) kiru in the -teru form: tsume kitteru.

modelAnswers.english: Right now? I'm cutting my nails.
I was cutting my nails. What's up?

questions.explanation: Cutting your nails is tsume o kiru, with the same kiru (cut) as kami o kiru. Kitteru is 'I'm cutting them right now'; kitteta is 'I was cutting them (until you called)'. Keep the double t: kiteru, with a single t, would be the 'wear' kiru. In the scene Kenta says tsume nagai yo, kittoki na yo (line 11), Sora says tsume kiranakya (line 12), and then tsume kitte, te mo aratta yo (line 14).

newWords.english: only, just (kami aratta dake = I just washed my hair)
girl, kid (ano ko = that girl, the one we both know about)
a meal, food (here: breakfast); also cooked rice
mom (okaasan ka yo = what are you, my mom?)
wear, put on (clothes); past kita. Not the kiru 'cut' (past kitta)
say (nan to iimashita ka = what did he say?)
